title: Security Trading Policy

tiers.name: Employees
tiers.description: Employees of the Company. May generally freely trade in Imdex securities, subject to Insider Trading law, a ban on short-term/speculative trading, a ban on derivatives (caps, collars, warrants or similar products), and restrictions on margin loans/collateral arrangements that give a lender a forced-sale right exercisable during a prohibited dealing time.

tiers.name: Key Management Personnel
tiers.description: Persons with authority and responsibility for planning, directing and controlling the Company's activities, including Directors and their associates, executives reporting directly to the Managing Director/CEO, and any other employees the CEO and Company Secretary consider appropriate. Subject to all Employee restrictions plus a written pre-approval requirement before any dealing and Closed Period/Prohibited Period bans.

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board has discretion to prohibit trading by any Key Management Personnel at any time, for example during periods relying on the Listing Rule 3.1A continuous disclosure exceptions (Prohibited Periods). Not expressly stated to be confidential; because KMP already need written approval to deal, the Board can exercise this by simply declining or conditioning an application rather than announcing a separate blackout.

rules.detail: Absolute, unconditional ban on derivatives over Imdex securities, naming 'collars' specifically, with no clearance carve-out, no venue limitation and no distinction by vesting status. Applies to Employees directly and to Key Management Personnel as an overlay on top of the Employee restrictions.
rules.evidence: not use derivatives such as caps, collars, warrants or similar products into in relation to any Company securities held by employees.

rules.detail: No separate 'hedging' definition exists; the derivatives ban (caps, collars, warrants or similar products) functions as the hedging prohibition and is absolute, with no vested/unvested distinction.
rules.evidence: not use derivatives such as caps, collars, warrants or similar products into in relation to any Company securities held by employees.

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named, but a prepaid forward or similar risk-transfer structure would likely fall within 'or similar products' in the derivatives ban, extending beyond the named caps/collars/warrants.
rules.evidence: not use derivatives such as caps, collars, warrants or similar products into in relation to any Company securities held by employees.

rules.detail: Short selling is not named anywhere in the policy.
CFDs are not named but function as a derivative 'similar' to the named caps/collars/warrants and so are treated as caught by the ban.
rules.evidence: not use derivatives such as caps, collars, warrants or similar products into in relation to any Company securities held by employees.

rules.detail: Margin loans are not banned outright; employees must exercise care and must not enter an arrangement that grants the lender a right to sell or compel sale of the securities at a time this policy prohibits the employee from dealing. A secured lender's actual exercise of forced-sale rights is separately listed as excluded from the policy's application.
rules.evidence: not enter into arrangements, such as margin loans or arrangements involving the Company's securities as collateral to secure repayment of a loan, where the lender is granted a right to sell or compel the sale of the securities at a time that this policy prohibits the employee dealing in the securities.

rules.detail: Offering securities as collateral is permitted but flagged as requiring care; not defined as a 'dealing' in its own right, so no clearance procedure is expressly attached to the act of granting security itself (as opposed to any resulting sale).
rules.evidence: exercise care if borrowing monies to purchase securities or offering securities held by them as collateral.

rules.detail: Secured financing arrangements using Company securities as collateral are permitted provided the lender is not granted a right to force a sale exercisable at a time when the employee is prohibited from dealing; the policy separately excludes an actual forced sale by a secured lender exercising its rights from the scope of the policy altogether, creating some internal tension.
rules.evidence: not enter into arrangements ... involving the Company's securities as collateral to secure repayment of a loan, where the lender is granted a right to sell or compel the sale of the securities at a time that this policy prohibits the employee dealing in the securities.

rules.detail: Absolute ban on short-term or speculative trading, defined as purchase and sale of the same securities within a 12-month period; no stated carve-outs.
rules.evidence: not engage in short term or speculative trading of Imdex Limited securities, which is defined as the purchase and sale of the same securities within a 12 month period.

clearance.evidence: Employees generally may freely trade in Imdex securities, however, they are reminded that Insider Trading restrictions apply to them.

clearance.approver: Chairman of the Board (via written application to the Company Secretary; Board informed of all requests and may be referred to for a decision, and must decide where the Chairman himself is the applicant)
clearance.post_trade_to: Company Secretary, who advises the Board and lodges an Appendix 3Y with ASX where applicable
clearance.post_trade_deadline: within five business days of the date trading occurred
clearance.evidence: Key Management Personnel must, on all occasions before dealing with the Company's securities, provide written notification to the Company Secretary ... The Company Secretary will then refer the application to the Chairman ... must respond ... normally, within 24 hours.

short_term.basis: purchase and sale of the same securities within a 12 month period
short_term.evidence: not engage in short term or speculative trading of Imdex Limited securities, which is defined as the purchase and sale of the same securities within a 12 month period.

exceptions.evidence: An application may be made to sell (but not to purchase) securities, when this policy otherwise prohibits, on the grounds of Exceptional Circumstances. "Exceptional circumstances" may include genuine hardship, severe financial hardship.
"Exceptional circumstances" may include ... court orders or some other overriding legal or regulatory requirement, as determined at the Chairman's discretion.
where the beneficial interest in the relevant Company's security does not change.
where the persons otherwise prohibited from dealing pursuant to this policy have no control over trading decisions.
trading under an offer or invitation made to all or most of the security holders ... undertakings to accept, or the acceptance of, a takeover offer.

an investment in, or trading in units of, a fund or other scheme (other than a scheme only investing in the securities of the entity) where the assets of the fund or other scheme are invested at the discretion of a third party.
a disposal of securities of the entity that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement.

the exercise (but not the sale of securities following exercise) of an option or a right under an employee incentive scheme ... where the final date for the exercise ... falls at a time prohibited under this policy and the Restricted Person could not reasonably have been expected to exercise it at a time when free to do so.

exemption_authority: Chairman of the Board has discretion to determine whether 'exceptional circumstances' justify approving a sale (never a purchase) during a Prohibited or Closed Period, may impose conditions, and must be satisfied the applicant holds no Material Inside Information; the Chairman must inform the Board of requests and must refer the matter to the Board where the Chairman is the applicant.

bespoke_clauses.clause: not use derivatives such as caps, collars, warrants or similar products into in relation to any Company securities held by employees.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The policy names 'collars' specifically as a banned derivative product over Company securities, so a bank-written funded collar (purchased put and written call) is expressly and unconditionally prohibited for Employees and, via the 'additional restrictions' overlay, for Key Management Personnel, with no clearance route available.

bespoke_clauses.clause: not enter into arrangements ... where the lender is granted a right to sell or compel the sale of the securities at a time that this policy prohibits the employee dealing in the securities [Employees item 4] versus a disposal of securities ... that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights ... is specifically excluded from the application of this policy [Scope of the Policy].
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The policy discourages granting a lender forced-sale rights exercisable during a prohibited dealing period, yet separately excludes the lender's actual exercise of such rights from the policy altogether; a bank relying on enforcement should seek company comfort given this internal tension, though it is moot for a collar structure because the hedge leg is independently and absolutely banned.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Will the transaction take place on the ASX (circle): YES/NO. If the transaction is not to take place on the ASX, advise details of the transaction.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The Key Management Personnel clearance application contemplates off-market/OTC transactions generally, showing the policy anticipates non-exchange dealings, but this administrative accommodation does not override the standalone, unconditional ban on derivative products.

bespoke_clauses.clause: take all reasonable steps to prevent the trading by their spouse, partner, child or other immediate family member, or trust or other entity controlled by them or an investment adviser on behalf of them intends dealing in Imdex securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Routing the collar or loan through a family trust or related entity does not avoid the derivatives ban, since employees must take reasonable steps to prevent associated persons from dealing on their behalf.

summary: A funded OTC equity collar is expressly prohibited under this policy: the Employees section bans the use of 'derivatives such as caps, collars, warrants or similar products' in relation to any Imdex securities held by employees, with no qualification by vesting status, venue or clearance, and this ban extends to Key Management Personnel (including Directors) as an 'additional restriction' layered on top of the ordinary Employee rules. Even disregarding the derivatives ban, Key Management Personnel could not deal without prior written Chairman approval (valid only 14 days, subject to conditions), and never during the half-year, year-end or AGM Closed Periods or a Board-declared Prohibited Period. The financing leg is only conditionally restricted: pledging Company securities as collateral requires 'care' and must not grant a lender a forced-sale right exercisable during a prohibited dealing time, though a secured lender's actual exercise of enforcement rights is separately excluded from the policy altogether. Because the derivatives prohibition is absolute and names 'collars' specifically, no tier or holding period can support a funded collar under this policy; at most, an unhedged secured loan carefully timed outside closed/prohibited periods might be considered, but the collar itself cannot be structured.
